why: Rule 8: all 14 clusters are sub-cm specks with no dQ/dx measured anywhere and no readable direction, so any click is as good as another; abstaining rather than inventing a reason.

Rule 1/5 combined: 17002 is the terminating end of the 451 cm forward muon and sits at the base of a diffuse EM fragment cloud (11 cm e prong plus 4.3 cm stub plus ~20 loose specks within 25 cm); no other candidate carries a long track, but rule 1 formally reads 0/3 so held below certain.
Rule 1 textbook: deg-3 with 3 of 3 segments rising away - 427 cm muon (x1.84), 8.3 cm proton to 188k (x1.45) and 15.1 cm pi+ (x1.36); zoom shows three well-separated green arrows, nothing collinear.

Only junction in the event and the most upstream candidate; zoom shows a clean 112 deg V with a 2x-MIP proton arm (34.8 cm, ending 128k) against a MIP muon arm that continues collinearly through clusters 71/42/69/70 and exits at z=500.

Rule 1: deg-3 where an 18.5 cm proton rises monotonically away to 194k, plus a hot 3.9 cm stub (131k) and the 65 cm pi+; the competing junction 15000 has the pi+ cooling away from it, and EM fragments sit 3 cm from 15002.

P4 shows the 21.7 cm proton rising monotonically on the template from 85k at 4003 to 220k at 4004, so it is born at 4003; 4005 is only a break on the muon (4003-4005 is collinear with 4005-4002 to 2 deg) and a Michel sits on the far end at 4002.
Rule 8: the entire event is two isolated sub-cm dots 66 cm apart with no dQ/dx measured on either, so there is no evidence to separate them; abstaining, same policy as evt179303.

Rule 1: deg-4 with two independent stopping protons pointing away - 39.1 cm rising to 178k (x2.30) and 17.7 cm rising to 210k (x2.21); rule 2 would pull ~93 cm upstream but is explicitly not allowed to overturn clear rule-1 evidence.

Rule 1: deg-3 where the 5.8 cm proton falls monotonically from 350k at its far end 1000 back to MIP at 1003 (born at 1003), joined by a second 3.5 cm 124k proton stub; the 91 cm prong is flat MIP and exits the top wall.

Only real object in the event is a 3.4 cm 6x-MIP proton stub with identical end means (shorter than the 5 cm window, so no direction); picked its low-z end by rule 2, which also faces the other three fragments 20 cm away. Close to a guess.

Rule 1: deg-3 with the 13.4 cm proton rising away to 213k, the 6.8 cm pi+ also hotter at its far end and the 281 cm muon leaving; the other deg-3 candidate 12004 is a 166 deg scatter kink inside one long track, i.e. the trap, and is discarded.

P4 shows seg 7011 rising monotonically along the proton template from 50k at 7004 to 320k at 7007, so the proton is born at 7004, which is also where the 128 cm muon attaches and the lowest-z candidate; dropped a tier because 7005 is a deg-4 junction only 4.3 cm away with its own stopping prong.
Rule 1: the 16.1 cm proton rises monotonically from 55k at 3002 to 290k at 3001 on the template, the 132 cm muon leaves at 123 deg (not back-to-back), and small EM fragments sit within 2 cm of 3002.

Deg-4 blob junction: the 4.3 cm proton falls 78k to 42k toward 11004 (born there) and both the 14.9 cm e prong and the 1.3 cm stub attach at 11004 only; held to likely because the mu and pi+ arms leave it collinear to 2 deg, which is trap 3.

Rules 6/7 on a shower-only event: 15001 is the narrow apex from which a single 37.7 cm trunk fans out into the ~30 cm wide fragment cloud at x < -60, and it is deg-3 carrying a short 1.7 cm 75k heavy stub plus a 2.5 cm stub; no track evidence anywhere, so not certain.
